title: Deep learning designs selective antimicrobial peptides against Cutibacterium acnes
summary: A deep-learning design pipeline combining sequence generation and classifiers, transfer learning, pretrained protein embeddings and C. acnes-specific training data produced 42 novel peptides for testing. Five showed high-potency, selective activity against C. acnes, with MICs of 2–4 µg/mL; additional in-vitro assays tested activity against other microbes, hemolysis and keratinocyte cytotoxicity.
ai_technology: Deep-learning peptide generators and activity/selectivity classifiers using transfer learning and pretrained protein embeddings
organization: Shanghai MetaNovas Biotech; Fuzhou University; Metanovas Biotech

evidence.tested: A deep-learning design pipeline combining sequence generation and classifiers, transfer learning, pretrained protein embeddings and C. acnes-specific training data produced 42 novel peptides for testing.
evidence.unknown: All evidence is in vitro, with no animal or human testing. The 42 synthesized candidates are a selected subset of model output, and the abstract's five high-potency peptides have measured C. acnes MICs; activity against other organisms and toxicity is based on separate in-vitro assays. Do not imply topical efficacy or clinical safety.
evidence.ai_role: The models generated peptide sequences, ranked antimicrobial/hemolytic properties and incorporated C. acnes-focused training data. The team synthesized and tested 42 selected designs; five had reported C. acnes MICs of 2–4 µg/mL.
